1  ORDER Mr.E.Balamurugan, learned Special Government Pleader takes notice for the respondents.
By consent of the parties, these main writ petitions are taken up for final disposal at the admission stage itself.

2. The petitioners are aggrieved against the proceedings of the first respondent dated 05.09.2018 imposing penalty on them under the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 along with Rules and Regulations, 2011.

3. Though these writ petitions are filed by raising very many grounds on merits of the matter opposing the punishment imposed on the petitioners as stated supra, this Court is not inclined to entertain these writ petitions on the sole reason that an appellate remedy is available to the petitioners before the Tribunal viz., Food Safety Appellate Tribunal, which has been clearly stated in the impugned orders themselves.
http://www.judis.nic.in 4

. However, the learned counsel for the petitioners submitted that the said impugned orders were received by the petitioners only on 14.01.2019 and to the petitioners' knowledge, the said Tribunal is not functioning.
Therefore, he contended that the present writ petitions can be entertained.

5. On the other hand, the learned Special Government Pleader for the respondents, based on instructions from the Food Safety Officer, Mr.S.Sasikumar, who is personally present before this Court, submitted that the Tribunal started to function from 01.02.2019 onwards and therefore, the petitioners can very well approach the Tribunal and file an appeal.

6. Considering the above stated facts and circumstances, these writ petitions are disposed of,
without expressing any view on the merits of the matter only with liberty to the petitioners to approach such Tribunal and file an appeal within a period of two weeks from the date of receipt of a copy of this order.

If any such appeal is filed, the same shall be considered by the Tribunal and orders shall be passed on merits and in accordance with law, as this Court is not expressing any view on the merits of the matter.

Till an appeal is filed before the http://www.judis.nic.in K.RAVICHANDRABAABU,J.
mk Tribunal, the respondents shall not take any coercive steps against the petitioners.
No costs.
Connected miscellaneous petitions are closed.
